title: Converos: Practical Model Checking for Verifying Rust OS Kernel Concurrency
problem: Verifying concurrent code in OS kernels is extremely difficult; traditional testing cannot guarantee the absence of race conditions, deadlocks, and other concurrency bugs in Rust OS kernel implementations.
motivation: OS kernel reliability and correctness are critical for system stability and security, yet concurrency bugs frequently evade traditional testing and code review.
method: Converos automatically tests all possible orderings of thread operations in concurrent kernel code to find bugs. To prevent this from taking forever, it uses abstraction (simplifying the code to just the essential parts) and reduction techniques (eliminating redundant checks) to cut down the number of execution paths that need checking. This makes automatic verification practical for real Rust OS kernels.
key_novelty: Using targeted simplification to manage the explosion of possible execution paths makes automatic verification practical for real Rust OS kernels.
contributions: A practical model checker for Rust OS kernels (Converos)
State-space reduction techniques for kernel-scale concurrent verification
Formal verification methodology applicable to production OS code
Demonstration of effectiveness on real Rust OS implementations
primary_theme: Model checking for concurrent OS kernel verification
